subject: Capacity scenarios and SKU catalog for Arboreal Dedicated commitment
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@arboreal.health>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@arboreal.health, sam.li@arboreal.health
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro — Dedicated capacity sizing for clinical inference workflow

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. We have a couple of pilots and an upcoming production rollout that will need dedicated capacity. High level: prediction service for clinical triage (avg request payload ~1.2k tokens, bursty spikes at 600 rps for 60s), and a chart-summarization endpoint (avg 4k tokens, long context).

Can you send a compact catalog of capacity scenarios (reserve/burst mixes) and clear guidance which SKU to pick for each workload (H100 vs A100 vs L4) — we need tradeoffs on memory headroom, latency percentile, and ops complexity. Also call out fallback model variants and estimated monthly committed spend for each scenario.

Procurement would like it in time for our internal review on Thursday.

Appreciate it —
Alex
Senior Engineering Manager, Arboreal Health

On Mon, Nov 20, 2026 at 15:40 Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Great to meet earlier, Alex. Will align scenarios with your 2 workload profiles and present cost/latency tradeoffs.
> Vivek
> Director, Deal Architecture — Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@arboreal.health>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, procurement@arboreal.health
Date: 2026-11-22T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity scenarios and SKU catalog for Arboreal Dedicated commitment

Alex — attaching a compact scenario catalog and simulation notes. High-level summary up front:

- Scenario A (Latency-first, production): H100 reserve pool sized for 99th pct < 120ms on 1.2k-token requests, long-context model split to L4-burst nodes for chart summarization. Ops notes: larger cache and KV lanes, higher cost (~$Xk/mo committed).
- Scenario B (Balanced): Mixed reserve (A100) for prediction + L4 for long tail. 95th pct < 180ms, smaller commitment. Good for moderate SLAs.
- Scenario C (Cost-first): L4-heavy with A100/H100 as burst fallback for peak. Optimized quantized variants, accepts 95th pct up to ~300ms. Lowest committed spend but more ops routing complexity.

Key tradeoffs we modeled: context length memory (L4 lower memory, faster small-context; H100 best for long KV + large-batch throughput), quantization compatibility (L4 supports more aggressive int8 paths; H100 preferred for FP16 large-context throughput), and slotting for burst vs reserve (tiling to increase effective concurrency on A100/H100).

Attachments: arboreal_capacity_scenarios_v1.xlsx (tabbed: assumptions, cost_estimates, failover_paths), latency_vs_cost_simulations.pdf (plots per request profile).

Questions for you before we finalize for Procurement:
1) Expected committed term (12 / 24 / 36 months)?
2) Any data residency/regulatory constraints beyond US region?
3) Tolerance for quantized output fidelity drops for chart summarization?

We’ll stand up a short runbook option for fast fallback (L4 -> A100 -> H100) if you want resilient latency tail behavior.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is already helpful. A couple quick clarifications:

- We’re leaning toward a 24-month commitment but need the cost delta between Scenario A and Scenario B expressed as percent uplift.
- Chart summarization fidelity: we can accept small (2–3%) degradation if latency improves significantly.
- Regulatory: all data must remain in US regions; we may want SOC2 evidence (can you point me to the standard artifact?).

Can you add a short table mapping model variant -> recommended SKU -> quantization path -> expected 95th percentile latency (per workload)? If you can get that by Wednesday evening we’ll include it in the procurement packet.

Cheers,
Alex

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@arboreal.health>, priyom_das@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, procurement@arboreal.health
Date: 2026-11-24T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity scenarios and SKU catalog for Arboreal Dedicated commitment

Alex — attaching an updated one-page mapping table in the workbook and callouts below. Deliverables are in Drive link: https://drive.redwood.internal/Arboreal/CapacityModel_v1 (see tabs: summary, model_map).

Short answers inline:
- Percent uplift (24-month commit): Scenario A vs B -> ~22% higher committed monthly spend, Scenario A buys ~2.4x headroom for long-context bursts. (See cost_estimates tab.)
- Model -> SKU mapping (summary):
  * prediction-service (1.2k tokens) -> A100 reserve (fp16) for steady throughput, H100 for dedicated p95-critical lanes; quantization: fp16 recommended for highest fidelity, int8 optional on A100 with controlled evals. Estimated 95th pct latency: A100 reserve ~110–170ms, H100 reserve ~70–110ms (depends on batching).
  * chart-summarization (4k tokens) -> H100 reserve preferred for large KV + long context; L4 can serve a quantized distilled variant for non-critical summarization with ~200–300ms p95 but has memory limits for 4k windows.
- SOC2: will send SOC2 Type II artifact via secure link; meanwhile, we can provide a SOC2 summary and audit point list for procurement.

Operational recommendation: start with Scenario B (A100 + L4) for month 1 production to reduce procurement friction, then schedule a Phase 2 upgrade to Scenario A if p95 SLA breaches are observed during the pilot. We’ll include automated routing policy to route high-confidence low-latency requests to L4 and high-fidelity/long-context to H100.

Next steps
- I’ll upload the SOC2 artifact and a brief runbook for fallback routing.
- Vivek/ Priyom: if you can prepare a short slide (1–2 pages) summarizing the mapping table and commit delta, Procurement wants it by Thursday EOD.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Product Lead — Dedicated Capacity, Redwood Inference
